properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Example Solana wallet's message-signing primitive: Ed25519 detached signatures over dapp messages (sign.detached, solanaWallet.ts:227). Deadline asset (forged signatures, not retroactive decryption); migrate to ML-DSA-65 after the key-exchange work. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA/ECDH available via elliptic@6.6.1, pulled by @ethersproject/signing-key@5.8.0 (ethers v5, declared by packages/example/wallets and packages/example/extension). No direct first-party elliptic import; the ECDH/ECDSA surface is exercised indirectly through first-party ethers Wallet calls (ethereumWallet.ts:68/163, extension wallet.ts:35). Presence in the shipped tree is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 half of the same tweetnacl usage: wallet-to-dapp message encryption (experimental:encrypt/decrypt). Retroactive (harvest-now-decrypt-later) exposure on recorded box ciphertexts; migrate to ML-KEM-768 hybrid. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (the pre-finalization SHA-3 variant Ethereum standardized on) shipped through the @ethersproject stack used by the two Ethereum wallets (packages/example/wallets/src/ethereumWallet.ts and the extension). Exercised first-party via ethers.utils.computeAddress for Ethereum address derivation, and inside Ethereum transaction hashing. Grover-only asset; the migration path is the Ethereum protocol itself, not this repo. Changeable here only by replacing the chain stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Symmetric authenticated encryption (XSalsa20 stream cipher + Poly1305 tag via HSalsa20-derived key) protecting wallet↔dapp messages. Grover-only; not a Shor asset — its quantum rating comes from the 256-bit key, not from key establishment. Changeable here only together with the X25519 half.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored crypto library in the shipped tree: elliptic@6.6.1 via @ethersproject/signing-key (ethers v5). Provides secp256k1 ECDSA signing/ECDH that backs every Ethereum key operation in the example wallets. No direct first-party import — reachable through ethers; availability is the inventory fact here.
